feedback.problem: Given that $x=5$ is a solution to the equation ${x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+29x-45=0,$ find the remaining solutions.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+29x-45.$ Since $x=5$ is a root of $f(x),$ then according to the factor theorem $(x-5)$ is a factor of $f(x).$ 

We find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x-5)$ using synthetic division.

$$
\begin{aligned}\enclose{bottom right}{5} & 1 & -9 & 29 & -45 \\  &  & 5 & -20 & 45 \\  & 1 & -4 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $f(x)=(x-5)({x}^{2}-4x+9).$ 

To find the remaining two roots, we solve ${x}^{2}-4x+9=0$ by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4x+9 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-4x+4+5 & =0 \\ (x-2)^{2}+5 & =0 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =-5 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =(\sqrt{5}\text{i})^{2} \\ x-2 & =\pm \sqrt{5}\text{i} \\ x & =2\pm \sqrt{5}\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to our original equation are $x=5,\,2\pm \sqrt{5}\text{i}.$
